export_controls.text:
What the Missouri Republican Congressional delegation has done for our farmers:

1) Stood by while USAID was “fed into the wood chipper” destroying one of our largest soybean export vehicles

2) Stood by while Trump imported 300k metric tons of bad ground beef in the middle of calf sales undermining the price for the 3rd largest beef producer state

3) Stood by while Trump started a trade war with our largest export partner, Canada.

4) Refused to approve, or even provide oversight, of an idiotic war with Iran that has blown up diesel prices during harvest.

5) Happily sold off swaths of our state to multibillion dollar tech companies for AI data centers with no oversight, regulations, or guardrails torching property values. 

Over and over @AnnLWagner and her Republican friends have chosen Trump and the corporations over our farmers. Enough is enough.

deepseek.reason: The statement discusses agricultural trade and AI data centers, not AI export controls.
deepseek.confidence_reason: No mention of AI chip, model, or compute export restrictions or enforcement.

china_race_dynamics.text: I keep being told we're in an AI arms race with China and we should shut up and let a trillion dollar+ industry simply roll into small towns and build whatever they want with no guardrails or regulations. China actually does regulate AI and is rapidly expanding their electric grid to support it. We're letting billionaires bully and bribe small towns into paying for their profits, water, and electricity while getting tax breaks and no limits on their power. We must help them. Working people shouldn't pay for their new yachts and be told its patriotism. Congress must do its part and I will.

deepseek.reason: The speaker rejects the AI arms race framing used to justify deregulating the industry in small towns.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Race skepticism and a demand for guardrails are clear, but the statement also notes China regulates AI, leaving some ambiguity about overall competition stance.

astra.reason: He challenges the AI arms-race framing used to demand deregulation and insists on protecting communities despite competitive pressure.
astra.confidence_reason: He clearly rejects the race-based justification for removing safeguards, though his rejection of competition itself is less explicit.

china_race_dynamics.text: China added over 543 Gigawatts to their grid last year. 434 GW was renewables because they are faster to build. The U.S. added a paltry 53 GW. We are losing the “AI race” to China because these idiots hate green energy. This is suicide by stupid. https://t.co/03YiK49Ccz

deepseek.reason: The speaker warns the US is losing the AI race to China and treats that competition as the frame for energy policy.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly adopts the AI race with China framing as its central claim.
